prompt: A payment key was committed, pushed, and deleted in the next commit. What comes first?
hint: Which step makes every copy harmless?

choices.text: Rewrite the history with git filter-repo and force-push it
choices.why: That tidies this repository and recalls no clone that already exists.

choices.text: Revoke the key at the provider and deploy a new one
choices.why: Right. From then on every copy of the history holds a dead key.

choices.text: Add the settings file to .gitignore
choices.why: That stops future commits of the file; the past commit is untouched.

choices.text: Delete the repository and push a fresh one
choices.why: Clones, forks and caches of the old one still hold the key.

prompt: Why is a key that reached a shared repository treated as known, even if nobody seems to have looked?
hint: Who has a copy of the history?

choices.text: Every clone, fork and cache already holds it
choices.why: Right. The copies are out of your reach, so the key is assumed to be too.

choices.text: Git publishes each commit to a public log of changes
choices.why: Git keeps history in the repository; nothing is published unless the repository is.

choices.text: Deleting a line takes days to reach the other clones
choices.why: A deletion is a new commit; the old commit stays in every copy regardless of time.

choices.text: The scanner sends each finding to the provider
choices.why: gitleaks reports to you, on your machine; it tells no provider anything.

prompt: Match each requirement of the test plan to what holds it.
hint: The table at the end of the first reading section.

pairs.left: no secret in any commit of the history
pairs.right: a history scan on every push

pairs.left: no secret in a commit to begin with
pairs.right: the same scanner on what is staged

pairs.left: the code holds no secret and no default for one
a found secret is rotated, not only deleted
pairs.right: the response procedure and its record

right_distractors: a DAST scan of the running service

prompt: In leaky, gitleaks dir reports no leaks and gitleaks git reports one in commit ad0a6bc. What does that say?

choices.text: The second scan is a false positive
choices.why: The key really is in ad0a6bc, as git show proved.

choices.text: An old commit still holds the key
choices.why: Right. dir reads the disk, git reads every commit.

choices.text: The deletion has not been committed yet
choices.why: It was: the log shows the second commit, and dir reads the file after it.

choices.text: gitleaks dir skips files ending in .ini
choices.why: It read settings.ini; there was simply no key left in it.

prompt: gitleaks stdin reports nothing for payment_api_key = "fake-7Zq2vRmX9kLp4Tn8Wc3Yb6Hd1Jf5G". Why?
hint: Change one word and it is reported.

choices.text: The value is too short for the generic rule
choices.why: The same length with another prefix is reported.

choices.text: Input from a pipe is checked by fewer rules
choices.why: The second line, also from stdin, is reported.

choices.text: It skips values that contain words like fake
choices.why: Right. So a test value has to look like a real key to be found.

choices.text: The name payment_api_key matches no rule
choices.why: It matched generic-api-key in settings.ini with a random value.

prompt: With its default settings, what exit code does gitleaks give when it finds a leak?
hint: The line after the findings in the history scan.

prompt: Which field of a finding names that one finding, so it can be recorded as dealt with?
hint: Commit, file, rule and line together.

choices.text: RuleID
choices.why: Many findings share a rule.

choices.text: Fingerprint
choices.why: Right. It joins commit, file, rule and line.

choices.text: Entropy
choices.why: A measure of randomness, the same for the same value anywhere.

choices.text: Commit
choices.why: One commit can hold several findings.

prompt: After *.env went into .gitignore, gitleaks dir still reported payment.env. Why is that right?
hint: dir and git answer different questions.

choices.text: The ignore rule takes effect after the next commit
choices.why: check-ignore showed it already applied; and dir does not consult it.

choices.text: payment.env had been committed before the rule
choices.why: It never was; the history scan still found only ad0a6bc.

choices.text: The key really is in a file on this disk
choices.why: Right. dir says what the machine holds, ignored files included.

choices.text: gitleaks reads .gitignore as a file of secrets
choices.why: The finding names payment.env, line 3, not .gitignore.

prompt: account.py was started with PAYMENT_API_KEY in its environment, as ana. Who can read the value from /proc/<pid>/environ?

choices.text: ana, who runs it, and root
choices.why: Right. The environment is protected as well as that account, and no better.

choices.text: Any user logged in to the machine
choices.why: nobody got Permission denied.

choices.text: Only root, through sudo
choices.why: ana read it with a plain tr, no sudo.

choices.text: No one, once the process has started
choices.why: The file holds the environment for the whole life of the process.

prompt: Which way of reading a payment key in Python is the one a tester should expect in review?
hint: What happens when the variable is missing?

choices.text: os.environ.get("PAYMENT_API_KEY", "nft7Zq2vRmX9kLp4")
choices.why: The default puts a key back in the file.

choices.text: os.environ["PAYMENT_API_KEY"]
choices.why: Right. A missing key stops the service at start-up instead of running with a key in the code.

choices.text: A value under [payment] in the committed settings.ini
choices.why: That is the leak this lesson started with.

choices.text: The ?key= parameter of each request
choices.why: An address is written into logs and history, as lesson 17 showed for tokens.

prompt: A service that stores secrets encrypted, gives each to the identity allowed to read it and records every read is a secret ___.
What does --staged make gitleaks read in the pre-commit hook?
hint: The hook runs before the commit exists.

choices.text: The whole history, from the first commit
choices.why: That is the pipeline's scan; in a hook it would be slow on every commit.

choices.text: Every file in the directory, ignored ones too
choices.why: That is gitleaks dir.

choices.text: The changes about to be committed
choices.why: Right. Only what this commit would add.

choices.text: The last commit that was pushed
choices.why: A hook before a commit has nothing to do with the last push.

prompt: The team installs the hook. Why does the pipeline still scan the history on every push?
hint: Where does the hook live, and what skips it?

choices.text: The hook reads fewer rules than the history scan
choices.why: The same gitleaks applies the same rules; it reads less input, not fewer rules.

choices.text: A pipeline scan is faster than a hook
choices.why: It is slower, reading every commit; speed is not why it exists.

choices.text: Hooks run only on the first commit of a clone
choices.why: The hook ran on every commit in leaky, and refused one.

choices.text: It lives in .git and --no-verify skips it
choices.why: Right. The bypass put a second leak in the history, and the scan caught it.

prompt: Why was git reset --hard HEAD~1 enough to remove the commit made with --no-verify?

choices.text: The key in that commit had been redacted
choices.why: --redact hides the value in gitleaks's output; the commit held the real value.

choices.text: It had never been pushed, so no copy existed
choices.why: Right. Once pushed, the first step would be rotation.

choices.text: reset also removes the commit from every clone
choices.why: reset changes this machine only.

choices.text: The hook ran again during the reset
choices.why: A pre-commit hook runs before a commit, not on a reset.

prompt: A real key was pushed to the shared repository. Put the response in order.
hint: Make the key worthless before anything else.
items: revoke the key at the provider and issue a new one
read the provider's log for uses of the old key
decide whether to rewrite the history
record the finding's fingerprint, with the reason

prompt: The pipeline's history scan has failed on every push for a month, over a key that was rotated on day one. What should the team do?
hint: Accept one finding, not the rule.

choices.text: Switch off the generic-api-key rule for the whole scan
choices.why: Then every new generic key passes too.

choices.text: Mark the scan job as allowed to fail in the pipeline
choices.why: A job that may fail reports nothing anybody reads, new leaks included.

choices.text: List its fingerprint in .gitleaksignore, with why
choices.why: Right. One commit, file, rule and line are accepted; every new finding still fails.

choices.text: Rotate the same key once more, then push again
choices.why: The scan reads the history, which rotation does not change.

prompt: A service reads its key from an environment variable. Which of these can carry the key out of it? Choose every one.
hint: Follow the copies, not the code.

choices.text: A helper script the service starts
choices.why: Right. A child process inherits the whole environment.

choices.text: A debug page that lists the environment
choices.why: Right. It prints the value to whoever opens it.

choices.text: The line os.environ["PAYMENT_API_KEY"] in the committed source code
choices.why: The code holds the name, not the value.

choices.text: An error tracker that captures the environment with each exception
choices.why: Right. The value travels with every report.

choices.text: Another user, without privileges, reading /proc/<pid>/environ
choices.why: nobody got Permission denied.

prompt: To check that a CI job received the database password, a colleague adds echo "$DB_PASSWORD" to it. What is wrong?
hint: Where does a job's output end up?

choices.text: echo strips the special characters out of the value
choices.why: Whatever it prints, it prints the secret into a log.

choices.text: CI variables are unreadable inside a job
choices.why: The job has to read it to use it.

choices.text: It writes the secret into the job's log
choices.why: Right. Show that it is set, for example its length, and never the value.

choices.text: The job leaks it to gitleaks, which keeps a copy
choices.why: gitleaks keeps nothing; the log is the leak.
